courses.title: Agriculture: The Foundation of Civilizations
courses.description: [GE 3B] Introduction to the genesis and evolution of agriculture as the foundation of civilizations throughout history. Analyzing agriculture within the context of the development and evolution of various civilizations over time. Emphasis on critical analysis of the historical development of agriculture in various parts of the world including the United States using documentary and literature collections. Open to all majors. Required of all College of Agriculture majors.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Food, Agricultural and Apparel Industries
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Socioeconomic and scientific issues in the Food, Agricultural, and Apparel Systems within a framework of moral philosophy and ethical reasoning. Analysis of topics in biotechnology in agricultural and apparel production, food processing, intellectual property rights, food safety, nutrition, the treatment of animals, the environment, labor rights in a global marketplace, and reducing world hunger and malnutrition.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Orientation and Careers in Animal Health Science
courses.description: Outline of the academic path that students will follow. Discuss the various employment opportunities available for students graduating with this degree. This class will cover campus life, university rules and regulations and administration. May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 3 units.
courses.prerequisites: AHS major.

courses.title: Handling, Restraint and Nursing Care of Domestic Animals
courses.description: General concepts of restraint and handling of wild and domestic animals. Emphasis is on physical, chemical and moral/psychological restraint. Discussion of the tools/equipment of restraint, rope work and medical problems that might occur during restraint. Corequisite(s): AHS 1129L .

courses.title: Handling, Restraint and Nursing Care of Domestic Animals Laboratory
courses.description: General concepts of restraint and handling of wild and domestic animals. Emphasis is on physical, chemical and moral/psychological restraint. Discussion of the tools/equipment of restraint, rope work and medical problems that might occur during restraint. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AHS 1129 .

courses.title: Clinical Anatomy and Physiology
courses.description: Familiarize students with the function and form of the animal body and its parts. A systems approach to prepare students to locate and recognize clinically significant anatomical features. The physiology will be taught as an organ system basis. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course and all other core curriculum courses to advance in the Animal Health Science program. May be taken up to three times for a total credit of 9 units. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course and all other core curriculum courses to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 2202L and AHS 2210 .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, BIO 1150 or BIO 115, BIO 1150L or BIO 115L, CHM 1210 or CHM 121, and CHM 1210L or CHM 121L.

courses.title: Clinical Anatomy and Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Familiarize students with the function and form of the animal body and its parts. A systems approach to prepare students to locate and recognize clinically significant anatomical features. Physiology will taught as an organ system basis. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course and all other core curriculum courses to advance in the Animal Health Science program Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course and all other core curriculum courses to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AHS 2202 and AHS 2210 .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, BIO 1150 or BIO 115, BIO 1150L or BIO 115L, CHM 1210 or CHM 121, and CHM 1210L or CHM 121L.

courses.title: Diagnostic Imaging
courses.description: How to safely and effectively produce diagnostic radiographs and ultrasonic images. Learn how to properly prepare and operate radiographic and darkroom equipment, computer radiography, as well as ultrasound equipment. Per department policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course and all other core curriculum courses to advance in the Animal Health Science program Corequisite(s): AHS 2208L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, AHS 1129 , and AHS 1129L .

courses.title: Diagnostic Imaging Laboratory
courses.description: Safely and effectively produce diagnostic radiographs and ultrasonic images. How to properly prepare and operate radiographic and darkroom equipment, computer radiography, as well as ultrasound equipment. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course and all other core curriculum courses to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AHS 2208 .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, AHS 1129 , and AHS 1129L .

courses.title: Veterinary Terminology
courses.description: Introduction to veterinary terminology and its usage in the veterinary field. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 2202 and AHS 2202L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS 1104

courses.title: Clinical Nutrition
courses.description: An introduction to basic nutrients and nutritional needs of well animals and the ramifications of disease conditions on the nutritional needs and clinical case management. Completion of the CVTEA required and recommended nutritional essential skills for veterinary technologists. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 115 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 115L or BIO 1150L ; CHM 121 or CHM 1210 and CHM 121L or CHM 1210L .

courses.title: Clinical Internship I
courses.description: Practical experience working in public or private clinics or laboratories where application of animal health sciences or research takes place. Experiences should be useful in preparation for state board exams in veterinary technology and/or AAALAC exams for certification in laboratory animal care. This course is intended for lower division students in the Animal Health Sciences major. This course is intended for lower division students in the Animal Health Sciences major.
courses.prerequisites: AHS 129 or AHS 1129 and AHS 129L or AHS 1129L .

courses.title: Dentistry Skills Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to the theories, practices, and techniques of small animal dentistry. Study of common oral diseases, routine and advanced dentistry procedures, and the role of the veterinary technician in dental care. Practical knowledge of general dentistry skills within the scope of a veterinary technician license. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AHS 3263 and AHS 3263L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS 3235 , AHS 3235L , AHS 2202 , AHS 2202L , AHS 1129 , and AHS 1129L .

courses.title: Laboratory Procedures and Clinical Pathology
courses.description: An advanced course providing instruction in hematology, clinical pathology, microbiology, and urinalysis used to diagnose health problems in veterinary clinics and diagnostic laboratories. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3235L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, BIO 1150 , BIO 1150L , CHM 1210 , AHS 2202 , and AHS 2202L .

courses.title: Laboratory Procedures and Clinical Pathology Laboratory
courses.description: An advanced laboratory course providing instruction in hematology, clinical pathology, microbiology, urinalysis and necropsy procedures used to diagnose health problems in veterinary clinics and diagnostic laboratories. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3235 .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, BIO 1150 , BIO 1150L , CHM 1210 , AHS 2202 , and AHS 2202L .

courses.title: Companion Animal Nursing and Surgical Skills
courses.description: Instruction on the nursing and surgical skills required to work with companion animals, mainly dogs and cats. How to safely restrain animals, how to use anesthetic and surgical equipment, and how to use proper aseptic technique. Preparation for common surgical procedures. Students must receive a C- or better to advance through the AHS program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3263L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 1129 / AHS 1129L , AHS 2202 / AHS 2202L , and AHS 3235 / AHS 3235L .

courses.title: Surgical Nursing Skills Laboratory
courses.description: Gain experience in the skills required to work in the veterinary surgical arena. Learn the different types of anesthetics used, surgical equipment, instruments and aseptic technique. Familiarize with the preparation for common surgical procedures. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3263 .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 3235 / AHS 3235L , AHS 2202 / AHS 2202L , and AHS 2208 / AHS 2208L .

courses.title: Parasitology and Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Animal parasites and pathogens and their relationship to clinical and subclinical parasitic diseases, as well as common diseases and disease processes of livestock, companion animals, laboratory animals and wildlife. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3305L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, AVS major, AG Science major, AG 1010 , or instructor permission; BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 ; and BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L .

courses.title: Parasitology and Infectious Diseases Laboratory
courses.description: Study of animal parasites and pathogens and their relationship to clinical and subclinical parasitic diseases, as well as common diseases and disease processes of livestock, companion animals, laboratory animals and wildlife. Per department policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AHS 3305 .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, AVS major, AG Science major, AG 1010 , or instructor permission; BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 ; and BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L .

courses.title: Clinical Pharmacology
courses.description: The use of clinical chemical procedures, the classification and action of pharmaceuticals, and the dispensing of medications will be studied. Includes conversion and calculation of drugs, prescription writing and routes of administration. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3307L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS 2202 , AHS 2202L , AHS 2208 , AHS 2208L , AHS 3235 , and AHS 3235L .

courses.title: Clinical Pharmacology Laboratory
courses.description: The use of clinical chemical procedures, the classification and action of pharmaceuticals, and the dispensing of medications will be studied. Includes conversion and calculation of drugs, prescription writing and routes of administration. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program Corequisite(s): AHS 3307 .
courses.prerequisites: AHS 2202 , AHS 2202L , AHS 2208 , AHS 2208L , AHS 3235 , and AHS 3235L .

courses.title: Lab Animal and Exotic Animal Medicine
courses.description: Instruction in laboratory and exotic animal medicine including husbandry, biological data, common diseases and conditions, research policy and procedures, and animal welfare. Corequisite(s): AHS 3369L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 104 or AHS 1104 , AHS 129 or AHS 1129 , AHS 129L or AHS 1129L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Lab Animal and Exotic Animal Medicine Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction on handling and restraint, identification, and common procedures of laboratory and exotic animals. Instruction includes concepts of laboratory animal facility management, personnel, quality assurance, animal welfare and husbandry. Emphasis is placed on the role of the veterinary technician. Corequisite(s): AHS 3369 .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 104 or AHS 1104 , AHS 129 or AHS 1129 , AHS 129L or AHS 1129L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Large Animal Medicine and Nursing Skills
courses.description: Instruction in large animal medicine and nursing. Advanced nursing and diagnostic techniques, response to disease, management of hospitalized patients, common diseases and conditions, and preventative medicine programs. Emphasis will be on the role of the veterinary technician in the veterinary hospital. Corequisite(s): AHS 4200L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 3263 , AHS 3263L , AHS 3307 and AHS 3307L .

courses.title: Large Animal Medicine and Nursing Skills Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction in large animal medicine and nursing skills. Hands-on experience with large animal species, including advanced handling and restraint, venipuncture, diagnostic testing and nursing care. Emphasis will be on the role of the veterinary technician in the veterinary hospital. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 3263 / AHS 3263L and AHS 3307 / AHS 3307L .

courses.title: Small Animal Medicine
courses.description: Instruction on small animal medicine. Advanced nursing and diagnostic techniques, response to disease, management of hospitalized patients, common diseases and conditions, intensive care, toxicology and preventative medicine programs. Emphasis will be on the role of the veterinary technician in the veterinary hospital.
courses.prerequisites: AHS 3235 , AHS 3235L , AHS 3263 , AHS 3263L , AHS 3307 , AHS 3307L , AHS 4407 , and AHS 4407L .

courses.title: Critical Care, Advanced Surgical Assisting and Anesthesiology
courses.description: Instruction in the specific concepts of intensive care veterinary nursing, surgical assisting in advanced and/or specialized surgical techniques and advanced anesthesia techniques will be mastered. Per department policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 4407L and AHS 4408L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 2202 , AHS 2202L , AHS 2208 , AHS 3263 , AHS 3263L , AHS 3307 , and AHS 3307L .

courses.title: Critical Care, Advanced Surgical Assisting and Anesthesiology Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction in the specific concepts of intensive care veterinary nursing, surgical assisting in advanced and/or specialized surgical techniques and advanced anesthesia techniques will be mastered. Corequisite(s): AHS 4407 .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 202 or AHS 2202 , AHS 202L or AHS 2202L , AHS 208 or AHS 2208 , AHS 208L or AHS 2208L , AHS 263 or AHS 3263 , AHS 263L or AHS 3263L , AHS 307 or AHS 3307 , and AHS 307L or AHS 3307L .

courses.title: Surgical Recovery, Nursing and Critical Care Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction in the specific concepts of intensive care, recovery and veterinary nursing of surgical and anesthetic patients. Corequisite(s): Animal Health Science major, AHS 4407 , and AHS 4407L .

courses.title: Clinical Internship II
courses.description: Practical experience working in public or private clinics or laboratories where application of animal health sciences or research takes place. Experiences should be useful in preparation for state board exams in veterinary technology and/or AAALAC exams for certification in laboratory animal care. This course is intended for lower division students in the Animal Health Sciences major.
courses.prerequisites: AHS 245 or AHS 2410 .

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Internship II
courses.description: Practical experience working in public or private clinics or laboratories where application of animal health sciences or research takes place. Experiences should be useful in preparation for state board exams in veterinary technology and/or AAALAC exams for certification in laboratory animal care. This course is intended for lower division students in the Animal Health Sciences major. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, and AHS 442 or AHS 4410 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics

courses.title: Veterinary Economics and Office Procedures
courses.description: Principles of veterinary economics and office procedures as they relate to companion animals. This will include medical record-keeping, navigation of practice management software, inventory and economic analysis, and electronic medical records. Client communication, team building and managing stress within a high stakes environment will be explored in depth. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, junior or senior standing, and AHS 2210 .

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: Synthesis of disease processes, including medical, pharmacological and nursing aspects of the disease. Preparation for the Veterinary Technician National Exam. Review of the Veterinary Practice Act with emphasis on veterinary technician scope of practice. Veterinary technician licensure, legal and continuing education requirements for licensure. Continued study of client communication, interpersonal skills, and veterinary professional mental health. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, senior standing, AHS 4407 , and AHS 4407L .

courses.title: Animal Industry and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Analysis of the application of science in the food animal industry and animal production systems, the role and use of food animals and animal products in resolving problems associated with humanity, and the influence of animal agriculture on history, civilization and human values.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Compendium
courses.description: [GE 5D] How the origins and evolution of the domestic dog and cat influence their behavior and unique nutritional requirements, how selection for desired traits leads to breed associated problems. Emergency first aid, nutrition, calculation of caloric requirements, common diseases, vaccines and the immune system, zoonotic diseases (diseases transmitted from animals to man.)
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Biology and Society
courses.description: [GE 5B] Fundamental concepts in biology are taught using socially relevant themes. Biological concepts are related to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow, exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigations, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society.

courses.title: Biology and Society Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] A laboratory support course applying lecture concepts through hands-on, inquiry-based, learn-by-doing approaches. Supports students in majors that require fundamental concepts of biology as they relate to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigation, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1110 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 1150 can be concurrent. Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Basic Microbiology
courses.description: A study of cell structure, function, metabolism, genetics, and diversity of microorganisms. The impacts of microorganisms on evolutionary, environmental and disease processes are discussed. Corequisite(s): BIO 2060L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Basic Microbiology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory techniques and methods used to study of cell structure, function, metabolism, genetics, and diversity of microorganisms. Identification and growth of microorganisms, as well as scientific thinking, are emphasized in the laboratory exercises. Corequisite(s): BIO 2060 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description: [GE 2] The theory and applications of real-valued functions, domain and range, compositions, inverses, transformations, equations and inequalities, and absolute value. Emphasis on polynomials, rational functions, power and root functions, piecewise functions, logarithms and exponential functions. Both symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, or C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Statistics with Applications
courses.description: [GE 2] Sample and population data; descriptive statistics, including numerical and graphical summarization of central tendency and spread; elementary probability, including events, basic probability rules, binomial and normal distributions; inferential statistics, including confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for one-population mean and proportion problems, simple linear regression and correlation
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
